enforcement.command: python tools/metthew_families.py --check (also planted in .githooks/pre-commit as Check 6d)
enforcement.still_open: F1..F7 judge the SHAPE of each claim. None of them runs a family's gate, so a gate that was never executed still passes. Until a family gate is run and its output stored, the catalogue describes intent, not a measured capability.

policy.one_vocabulary: A capability id is defined exactly once in this file (shared[] or a family's capabilities[]). A shard manifest may only declare ids listed here. Enforced by F1/F2 in tools/metthew_families.py, and by tests/test_metthew_families.py for the manifests that exist.
policy.partition: affects=sim work must be determinism=exact (validator V7, catalogue F2). affects=presentation may be approximate (V9 then forces golden_run.headless=true), and presentation work may still be exact when the selection itself is reproducible from integers.
policy.tier_budget: tier highend: up to 8 GiB and 1024 files (HIGHEND_PAYLOAD_CAP / HIGHEND_FILE_CAP in tools/metthew_validate.py). The low-end contract is 2 MiB and 24 files. The families below are chosen so that the shard's BYTES are recipes, latents and transcripts, not baked assets: a high-end shard should be small even when it looks enormous.
policy.no_claim_without_a_gate: Every family carries acceptance.gate (a command plus a number it prints) and acceptance.negative_control (an input that MUST fail). A family without both is a wish. F3 refuses it; neither the checker nor the tests can assert that a gate was ever run.
policy.lineage_tiers: Every lineage entry carries source_tier. A = the artefact's own page or paper, fetched and read (url + fetched_on, or a repo-relative path to this estate's own primary document); B = an official index or registry entry (url); C = credible secondary reporting, fetched (url + fetched_on); D = a search snippet, social post or unread link -- a LEAD, not evidence, and it must say which kind in evidence. --check prints how many entries are checkable and how many are leads.
policy.payload_claim: No byte figure without a measurement. payload_bytes_estimate is refused by name (F5); a family either says status=measured with bytes + command + measured_on, or status=unmeasured with a reason. An invented size is a wish with a unit.

shared.note: positions and velocities in integer millimetres; no float reaches the authoritative state
aim resolved by integer sign comparison, never by atan2 -- an angle would import a platform libm into the hash
the golden input is a fixed byte log decoded by a branch-free rule; no clock, no ambient entropy
sha256 over one explicitly ordered string, never over a repr, a dict or a set
LCG on integers with the seed in the input transcript; the stream is part of the state
declared, not implemented by the reference shards: the field marks where a renderer sits, and V9 forces the golden hash to be taken headless
collision read from a 1-bit integer grid so that captured or neural scenery can still be played exactly
GGRS-style rewind and resimulate; only meaningful because the state is integer-only
the authoritative tick runs at sim_hz regardless of the presented frame rate
a 1280x720 frame drawn from the integer state; a --headless run changes nothing in the hash
positions, velocities and hit tests are integer; no float reaches the authoritative state
sprites are generated at run time from the integer state; no external image assets in the payload
PCM tones are generated at run time; no external audio files in the payload
one arena and its obstacles are encoded in the shard; no external level data
a fixed hex input log is decoded by a branchless rule; no clock, no ambient entropy
sha256 over one hand-written canonical string; dict and set order are never used

families.name: GLASSLAND -- virtualised geometry sandbox
families.pitch: Ship the decomposition, not the model. The shard carries a cluster DAG and micro-tiles; the host cuts the visible set every frame from a trillion-triangle scene.

lineage.source: Epic, Nanite Virtualized Geometry in Unreal Engine (UE 5.8 documentation)
lineage.adaptation: a cluster graph is data, so it can be content-addressed and diffed like any other shard file

lineage.source: NVIDIA RTX Mega Geometry, GDC 2026 (BVH builds for cluster-based geometry)
lineage.evidence: search-snippet (Tom's Hardware, 2026-05-09, describes the GDC 2026 announcement); the vendor page itself was not fetched
lineage.adaptation: the reference shard ships the geometry source, not the BVH: the BVH is rebuilt per host, so it never has to be shipped or trusted

lineage.source: Arm, 'Mali and Unreal Engine's Nanite'
lineage.adaptation: GPU-driven culling runs on integrated silicon, so the high-end family is not a discrete-GPU-only family

lineage.source: ACM, 'Real-time Path Tracing of Massive Dynamic Foliage'
lineage.adaptation: the cut is a function of the camera cell (integer), so two players in the same cell get the same cluster set -- reproducible selection, approximate pixels

capabilities.note: visible cluster set computed from an integer camera cell and an integer LOD level; identical on any host that runs the same cut, which is what makes a peer's screenshot reviewable
the rasterised result is vendor-approximate by design; it never enters the state hash

families.payload_shape: cluster DAG (quantised vertex/index blocks) + micro-UV tiles; the same scene as a shipped mesh set is 10-100x larger

payload_claim.reason: no cluster DAG has been cut on this box; the builder for this family does not exist yet, so any number would be arithmetic about a file nobody made

host.gpu: mesh-shader or compute-capable; works on integrated silicon (Nanite-on-Mali class)
host.fallback: the sim half of the shard still runs on python-resident; the geometry half degrades to flat-shaded boxes

acceptance.gate: two hosts run the same camera cell + LOD level and print the same cluster-cut hash, while the frame's pixel hash is allowed to differ
acceptance.negative_control: a shard whose cluster DAG was cut from a different scene must produce a different cluster-cut hash (a gate that returns the same answer for any DAG proves nothing)

families.name: SPECTRA -- neural-compressed material shard
families.pitch: Ship a latent, not a texture set. The shard carries a small network plus a compressed feature grid; the host reconstructs the full PBR stack for the material it is asked for.

lineage.source: NVIDIA RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK, D3D12 Cooperative Vectors path
lineage.evidence: not-located-in-this-session; the technique is corroborated by the HPG 2025 paper cited below, the SDK page is not
lineage.adaptation: an all-PBR-at-once codec is exactly the unit a shard ships: one file, one material, one address

lineage.source: Intel, Cooperative Vectors demo (PBR set compression)
lineage.adaptation: the technique is not vendor-locked, so the family is declared with a portable decode path and a native fast path

lineage.source: Belcour & Benyoub, 'Hardware Accelerated Neural Block Texture Compression with Cooperative Vectors' (HPG 2025, arXiv 2506.06040)
lineage.adaptation: reconstruction quality is measured per material, which turns 'does it look right' into a number a gate can refuse; the abstract reports a 4k PBR set (9 channels) rendered with anisotropic filtering at 1080p in 28 MB, which is the kind of figure this family's gate has to beat or admit it lost to

capabilities.note: reconstruction is vendor-approximate; the shard declares the tolerance it was validated at
the gate's measuring stick: decoded material vs the reference set, per channel, at a declared resolution

families.payload_shape: MLP weights (quantised) + latent feature grid; the paper's own result is 28 MB for a 4k set, so a shard in the low tens of MB is plausible and has not been measured here

payload_claim.reason: no latent has been trained; the 28 MB figure belongs to the cited paper's setup, not to anything this estate produced

host.gpu: cooperative-vector fast path; scalar fallback decode keeps the shard readable
host.fallback: scalar decode at 1-4 fps per material, enough to verify a shard on a laptop

acceptance.gate: decoded material at the declared resolution reaches the declared per-channel PSNR against the reference set, and the latent file is under 5% of that set's bytes
acceptance.negative_control: a latent trained on a different material must MISS the PSNR threshold -- if it passes, the threshold is measuring the harness, not the shard

families.name: FOGCUT -- path-traced, no bake
families.pitch: Ship a lighting recipe instead of a lightmap. The shard carries a sampling sequence, a seed and a per-tier sample budget; the player's own GPU converges the image.

lineage.source: NVIDIA RTX innovations at GDC 2026 (path tracing, Shader Execution Reordering, Mega Geometry)
lineage.evidence: search-snippet for the Mega Geometry announcement only; the SER material was not located
lineage.adaptation: SER makes incoherent rays affordable, so a shard can declare 'unbaked, path traced' without demanding a halo product

lineage.source: ACM, 'Real-time Path Tracing of Massive Dynamic Foliage'
lineage.adaptation: the recipe travels with the scene; foliage is no longer the reason a shard needs a baked atlas

capabilities.note: seed + low-discrepancy sequence + spp budget; the recipe is bytes, the image is the host's
every frame is a valid image and every further frame is closer; a screenshot's spp is part of its claim

families.payload_shape: sky/lights description + sampling recipe + seed; the lightmap it replaces is measured in hundreds of megabytes

payload_claim.reason: no recipe has been authored, and the 'hundreds of megabytes' it is compared against is a range about other projects' lightmaps, not a measurement of one here

host.gpu: hardware ray tracing; the shard degrades to a rasterised approximation below the declared tier
host.fallback: headless CPU trace at low spp for verification only

acceptance.gate: at the declared spp, the converged frame is within a stated error of a 64-spp reference frame of the same recipe
acceptance.negative_control: a frame rendered with a different seed must fall OUTSIDE that error band -- otherwise the band is wider than the effect it is supposed to detect

families.name: SPLATFIELD -- capture-derived playfield
families.pitch: Nobody models the map: a circle member captures a real place and the shard carries a pruned splat set for scenery plus an integer occupancy grid for play.

lineage.source: Kerbl, Kopanas, Leimkuhler & Drettakis, '3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering' (arXiv 2308.04079, SIGGRAPH 2023)
lineage.adaptation: the abstract claims >= 30 fps novel-view synthesis at 1080p for unbounded scenes, which is the claim the second-life kit relies on; the '100-200x faster than 2020 NeRF baselines' figure this entry used to quote is a survey number and is NOT in the paper, so it is dropped rather than repeated

lineage.source: Splat-based reconstruction in engine pipelines
lineage.adaptation: splats render but do not collide, so the shard ships a second, integer artefact: the occupancy grid the sim actually uses

capabilities.note: sorted-by-depth rendering is approximate; the sort key is integer-quantised so the ORDER is stable
a 1-bit-per-voxel grid derived from the capture; collision is grid lookup, so a captured room plays identically on every host

families.payload_shape: pruned splat set (position/scale/rotation/colour, quantised) + occupancy grid RLE

payload_claim.reason: no capture has been processed on this box; a splat count per room would be a guess with a byte suffix

host.gpu: splat rasteriser; the occupancy half runs anywhere

acceptance.gate: the occupancy grid reproduces the reference collision trace for 128 scripted probes, exactly
acceptance.negative_control: a grid derived from a different capture must fail at least one probe -- a grid that collides with everything passes every trace

families.name: MIRRORCAST -- rollback netcode with a verification ledger
families.pitch: Predict, resimulate, and prove. Rollback is affordable because the state is integers, and every claimed run carries a transcript any peer can replay.

lineage.source: GGRS / GGPO rollback netcode (gschup/ggrs)
lineage.evidence: not-fetched-this-session; the repository is named from prior knowledge, not from a page read today
lineage.adaptation: rollback requires an exactly reproducible step, which is the same requirement the golden run already imposes -- so the two features share one gate

lineage.source: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference (arXiv 2601.17768); cited previously as 'verified speculation, SOSP 2026'
lineage.evidence: search-snippet; the SOSP 2026 venue this entry used to claim could NOT be confirmed, so the venue is withdrawn and the arXiv preprint stands alone
lineage.adaptation: the idea, not the code: speculate ahead, then verify against the authoritative input and roll back on mismatch -- applied to frames instead of tokens

lineage.source: Deterministic simulation testing (2024-2026 practice)
lineage.evidence: not-located-in-this-session; a practice, not a document
lineage.adaptation: a shard's CI is a transcript replay, not a screenshot comparison

capabilities.note: GGRS-style rewind and resimulate; only meaningful because the state is integer-only
each speculative tick records the input it assumed; a mismatch invalidates from that tick forward, and the ledger is the evidence

families.payload_shape: code + golden transcript; the ledger is produced at play time, not shipped

payload_claim.reason: code-only family and no rollback shard exists: there is no transcript to measure. The manifest that describes one (fixtures/valid_highend_rollback_duel.json) is a manifest, not a game

host.fallback: n/a -- this is the family every host can run

acceptance.gate: two peers replaying the same transcript produce identical state hashes after a forced 12-tick rollback
acceptance.negative_control: an approximate value injected into the sim (a float position) must break hash equality; if it does not, the state is not being hashed

families.name: PERSONA -- on-device characters, subordinate to the sim
families.pitch: The shard ships a persona card, not a model. The host's small language model may propose, but only an enumerated intent can change the world, and that intent is written into the input log.

lineage.source: NVIDIA on-device small language model for game-character roleplay
lineage.adaptation: the model is a HOST capability; the shard's asset is the character definition, so a shard never carries gigabytes of weights

lineage.source: Braas & Esterle, 'Fixed-Persona SLMs with Modular Memory: Scalable NPC Dialogue on Consumer Hardware' (arXiv 2511.10277)
lineage.adaptation: persona is a small bounded card + a runtime-swappable memory module; that is exactly the shape a content-addressed file can hold, and it is the paper's own structure rather than an inference from its title

lineage.source: Arm, 'First Contact: a mobile architecture for LLM-powered game characters'
lineage.adaptation: the LLM is kept subordinate to game logic; prose never mutates state directly

capabilities.note: traits, refusal rules and memory schema; dialogue text is approximate and excluded from the hash
the only channel from language to world: a fixed enumerated action set, recorded in the transcript, so replay needs no model at all

families.payload_shape: persona card (a few kB) + memory schema + intent table

payload_claim.reason: no persona card has been authored; 'a few kB' is a shape, and the family ships no file to weigh

host.gpu: any on-device inference host; a 1-4B SLM is enough
host.fallback: deterministic scripted lines when no model is present -- the shard must remain playable, which is what makes the model optional

acceptance.gate: replaying a recorded transcript with the language model DISABLED reproduces the identical state hash
acceptance.negative_control: an intent outside the enumerated set must be rejected and logged, not silently coerced -- a gate that accepts every intent cannot tell a jailbreak from a move

families.name: NEURALFRAME -- interpolation that lifts the low end
families.pitch: The high-end feature is used downward: a 30 Hz deterministic sim is presented at 120 Hz by local frame interpolation, so a weak laptop feels smooth without changing what happened.

lineage.source: Frame generation / DLSS-class interpolation in shipped games
lineage.evidence: not-located-in-this-session; an industry practice rather than one document
lineage.adaptation: because the sim is integer and dual-rate, interpolation can never desynchronise gameplay from what was simulated

lineage.source: Thinking Machines Lab, 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' (2025-09-10); cited previously as arXiv 2609.25624, which could not be located
lineage.evidence: search-snippet; the arXiv id this entry used to cite (2609.25624) does not resolve to a locatable paper, so it is withdrawn
lineage.adaptation: the same move at shard scale: declare the reduction/tile order in the manifest, so cost and result depend on shape, not on scheduling

capabilities.note: n interpolated frames between two authoritative ticks; the declared n is part of the presentation claim
the authoritative tick runs at sim_hz regardless of the presented frame rate

families.payload_shape: code only; interpolation is a host technique with a declared parameter

payload_claim.reason: code-only family and no interpolator has been written; there is no file to weigh

host.gpu: any compute-capable GPU; historically this is the family that ran on the weakest box
host.fallback: no interpolation: 30 Hz presented as 30 Hz, with the same state hash

acceptance.gate: with interpolation on and off, the state hash after 600 ticks is identical; only the presented frame count differs
acceptance.negative_control: an interpolator fed a stale tick must be detected by the tick stamp check, not produce a plausible wrong frame

families.name: LADDER -- declared intensity tiers
families.pitch: High-end is not only fidelity, it is frame-time discipline. The shard declares the tiers it ships, what each tier removes, and each tier has its own golden run.

lineage.source: Nanite-on-Mali and the mobile-GPU trend
lineage.evidence: not-located-in-this-session; the same unlocated Arm material as GLASSLAND's third entry
lineage.adaptation: the same content must scale from a handheld to a desktop, so the tier ladder is a shard artefact, not a settings menu bolted on later

lineage.source: Measured hardware variance in this estate (Arc 140T, total_memory 7.80 GB via torch.xpu.get_device_properties)
lineage.adaptation: tiers are declared against measured memory and frame budgets, not against marketing names

capabilities.note: the tier is selected by integer comparison against a declared budget, so the same host picks the same tier every run
each tier states what it drops; dropping something undeclared is a contract violation, not an optimisation

families.payload_shape: levels file + code; the ladder is the cheapest family to ship and the one that makes the others honest

payload_claim.command: python -c "import json,pathlib; m=json.loads(pathlib.Path('docs/METTHEW/reference-shards/highend_ladder/shard.json').read_text()); print(sum(f['size_bytes'] for f in m['files']))"
payload_claim.note: the reference shard IS this family's payload: main.py 11540 + SHARD.md 3804 bytes. This is the only family whose size is a measurement rather than a shape.

host.fallback: n/a -- the lowest tier is the fallback

acceptance.gate: every tier replays the same transcript to the SAME state hash, while the tier's presentation counters differ (proved by reference-shards/highend_ladder --verify)
acceptance.negative_control: a tier allowed to change the sim must break hash equality -- if it does not, the ladder is secretly mutating the game
